sets.title: Assassin's Creed
sets.statusNote: Built from research, waiting for a player report.
notes: Vault reads the save headers in %APPDATA%\Ubisoft\Assassin's Creed\Saved Games and never touches the game. The game saves on its own as you play.

Untested: "Nothing Is True" works as soon as the game has saved once. The Memory Block achievements depend on the save header naming the block, which Vault hasn't been able to check on a real save yet. If they don't pop, send a test report.
The Places achievements count when a save header names the city you're in; also unchecked on a real save.

notes: Campaign achievements come from your save games (Vault never touches the game, which has online play). The game saves automatically between missions; saving during a mission helps too.

Skirmish achievements come from the replay the game saves after every game (Documents\Red Alert 3\Replays). Replays do not record who won, so these are about playing, not winning. Games shorter than 3 minutes do not count.

sets.title: Diablo
sets.statusNote: Save reading confirmed on a real character.
notes: Works with any copy of Diablo: Battle.net, GOG, the original CD, and DevilutionX. Hellfire too.
Vault reads your save files and never touches the game. Single-player progress counts when the game saves: use Save Game in the menu, and achievements pop up then.
Multiplayer heroes save all the time, so their achievements pop almost straight away.
Kills and quests come from the saved game, so they're counted per hero and added up across all your heroes.

sets.title: Hearthstone
sets.statusNote: Log reading checked on sample Hearthstone logs; waiting for a player report.
notes: Hearthstone is online, so Vault never reads its memory. Achievements come from Hearthstone's own game log (Power.log), the same one Hearthstone Deck Tracker reads.
Vault turns the game log on for you (it adds a [Power] section to Hearthstone's log.config). If Hearthstone was open when you installed or updated Vault, restart it once.
Games played before the log was on can't count. Class wins count from your first logged game.

sets.title: Heroes of the Storm
sets.statusNote: Read correctly from 52 real replays (heroes, maps, score screen, awards); live popup after a new match not confirmed yet.
notes: Heroes of the Storm runs Blizzard's anti-cheat, so Vault never reads its memory or touches its files. Achievements come from the replay Heroes saves after every match (Documents\Heroes of the Storm\Accounts\...\Replays).
Your old replays count too: the first time Vault starts with this set it goes through every saved replay and unlocks what you've already earned, dated to when you played, without a flood of popups.
Achievements pop when the score screen appears, not during the match.
If several people play on this PC, Vault counts the account with the most replays. You can pick another in Settings → Heroes of the Storm.
Hero and battleground names come from the replay in the game's language; per-hero and per-map achievements currently match the English names.

sets.title: Star Wars: Empire at War
sets.statusNote: Save reading confirmed on a real Forces of Corruption save.
notes: Empire at War has online play, so Vault never reads its memory. It reads your save games in Saved Games\Petroglyph.

The galactic map save holds the whole campaign script, so it can only show which campaign you started. Story battles are different: save once during each story battle (Esc, Save) and Vault records it.
Covers the Rebel and Empire campaigns and the Forces of Corruption campaign with Tyber Zann.
Every save also names its tutorial or Galactic Conquest map, so tutorials and Galactic Conquest games count as soon as you save once in them (wins are not recorded in saves).

sets.title: StarCraft: Remastered
sets.statusNote: Replay reading and results confirmed live.
notes: StarCraft: Remastered ships with Blizzard's anti-cheat, so Vault never reads its memory. Achievements come from the replay StarCraft writes when every match ends (Documents\StarCraft\Maps\Replays), parsed with screp (Apache-2.0).
Achievements pop on the score screen when a match ends, not during play.
Your player is found by name (Settings → StarCraft player name) or, in games with just one human, automatically.
Unit, building and research achievements count what you ordered, as recorded in the replay.
Your last game counts even if Vault was closed while you played (StarCraft keeps the last replay).

Campaign missions: StarCraft keeps campaign progress on Blizzard's servers, so Vault learns it from your save games. Save a game once in each new mission (Menu, Save Game) and the missions before it count as beaten.

sets.title: Warcraft III: Reforged
sets.statusNote: Campaign chapters confirmed; skirmish, Hard and secret level untested.
notes: Warcraft III has Blizzard's anti-cheat, so Vault never reads its memory. Achievements come from the campaign progress file the game saves in Documents\Warcraft III when you beat a chapter.
Achievements pop on the victory screen, as soon as the game saves your progress. Progress you already have counts too.
Campaign on Hard: set the difficulty to Hard before you play the chapter. Chapters you beat before Vault was watching do not count as Hard.
Skirmish and lifetime achievements come from the replay Warcraft III saves after every game (LastReplay.w3g). Turning on "Auto-save replays" in Options keeps every game, so none are missed.
